data.text: Marcus, anesthesia reviewed the schedule and Wednesday will not work. The earliest available slot moved to Thursday, March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival.

prior_context.speaker: scheduler_terry
prior_context.text: At the moment, yes: Wednesday morning, 8:50 arrival for a 10:20 procedure. Any clinical questions need to go through Marcus.

prior_context.speaker: agent_memcare
prior_context.text: Scheduling note: logistics-only family access still active through Monday. Current tentative slot is Wednesday March 11, 8:50 AM arrival for 10:20 AM procedure in cardiac procedures.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Marcus, this is Klein from cardiology pharmacy. I am calling to make sure the new metoprolol dose is clear.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: You are moving to 37.5 milligrams twice daily. Since you have 25-milligram tablets, that means one and a half tablets in the morning and one and a half tablets in the evening.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: And apixaban stays 5 milligrams twice daily, no holding it before the procedure unless the cardiologist specifically tells me?

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Exactly. Do not stop or skip apixaban on your own. The only routine hold we discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Also, magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for five nights, and no ibuprofen or naproxen while you are on apixaban.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Thanks. Please do not call the Cedar Bridge number unless my cell fails.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Documented. I only needed the medication plan and contact preference, not any other social details.

states.content: Over the past week Marcus Reed has had chest fluttering most evenings, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and one episode of lightheadedness on Saturday; he did not pass out. He also reports no chest pain and no bleeding, but has a racing heartbeat and feels washed out. His presentation is characterized as symptomatic atrial fibrillation/flutter with exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness, and no active bleeding. Clinician Dr. Patel confirms he is still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response but is stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan. He had shoulder pain last week, for which he took ibuprofen a couple of times before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list. Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Dr. Patel has now instructed Marcus to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and to use acetaminophen instead if needed, because NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with apixaban. Pharmacist Klein reinforced this: no ibuprofen or naproxen while Marcus is on apixaban. Marcus reported he has not missed any morning apixaban doses and no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers; he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations but still took that pill before bed. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Marcus does not drink energy drinks.
